messages:
tori_sales: MerchantX wants to swap off CompetitorY next month. Need a quick POC cutover runbook — tech + security + pricing alignment. Proposed POC window May 15-19. Who can own infra smoke + fallback plan?

jamal_se: I can lead the infra smoke. Key items: prompt-parity tests, response-schema normalization, rate-limit mapping, auth header differences. Note: CompetitorY uses X-Client-Id; we use Bearer tokens. We'll provide an adapter shim for header mapping.

sam_infra: Adapter shim sounds fine. Two infra blockers to flag: 1) MerchantX wants BYOK/KMS access (HSM requirement?) and 2) static egress IPs for their allowlist. @lisa_security will need to confirm acceptable KMS model.

lisa_security: Security checklist: confirm SAML/SSO, vendor questionnaire (data retention, encryption at rest+transit, logs access), and key management. I'll send the questionnaire with tickboxes. For KMS: Hosted can use separation-of-keys; Private/Dedicated supports customer-managed HSM-backed KMS. :lock:

jamal_se: For parity tests, quick smoke curl. Note a behavioral diff: CompetitorY auto-trims trailing newline and enforces default stop token; Redwood returns raw tokens unless you set stop. Example: ```bash
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"prompt":"Summarize this into one sentence:\nInput...","max_tokens":120,"stop":"\\n"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Use stop to match trimming behavior. Also watch sampling: top_p/top_k differences affect length.

ophelia_support: I'll coordinate the sample prompt set and the eval harness. Ask MerchantX for 50 canonical prompts + 20 known failure cases (edge prompts). ETA to prep harness: 3 business days after prompts received.

tori_sales: Buyer asked about pricing parity — CompetitorY bills per response chunk; MerchantX needs a visible estimate. @jamal_se can you generate expected token counts for their sample prompts?

jamal_se: Yes — will run tokenization and produce a token-cost spreadsheet. FYI response deltas can change token counts; to approximate brevity we can suggest using sampling at top_p=0.7 vs competitor's top_p=1.0. Also include microbenchmarks for latency.

lisa_security: Legal asks: data residency, SLA (they want 99.9%), SOC2. We have SOC2; Dedicated/reserved capacity offers SLA add-on. I'll route contract + security notes to legal.

sam_infra: Canary idea: proxy 1% traffic to Redwood and 99% to CompetitorY, log both responses, and run diffs for content + latency. Need a proxy that does parallel calls and stores side-by-side results. Will also produce required static IPs.

jamal_se: Our staging routing supports parallel-call mode (aka dual-run). We'll produce a merge/diff report and a JSON diff tool to surface semantic deltas. Also callout: CompetitorY had stateful session tokens; our API is stateless unless you use session endpoints — document handshake and session mapping.

tori_sales: Action items and due dates: jamal_se -> parity test harness + token estimate (due 1707920000). sam_infra -> canary proxy config + static IP list (due 1707800000). lisa_security -> send questionnaire + security sign-off (due 1707765000). ophelia_support -> collect prompts from MerchantX and start eval. I'll sync with MerchantX CSM.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Created ticket INFRA-7812 for canary proxy. Assignee: sam_infra. Link: https://redwood.atlassian/INFRA-7812

ophelia_support: MerchantX confirmed prompt set delivery tomorrow and will share a sample of their traffic patterns/logs. :thumbsup:

tori_sales: Great — weekly check-in Friday 10am PT. If any blockers pop, ping #release-war-room. :eyes:
